# SPI Host Module Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

This module is a SPI host controller. It provides a memory-mapped programming interface for software to issue SPI transactions, control chip-select and clock timing, exchange data with SPI target devices, and report status, events, and errors.

The module supports:

- Standard SPI, Dual SPI, and Quad SPI transfers.
- Multiple chip-select outputs, with per-chip-select configuration.
- TX and RX data FIFOs accessed through the register interface.
- Configurable SPI clock polarity, phase, and sampling timing.
- Multi-segment commands with chip-select held active between segments.
- Pass-through operation, where the SPI output pins are controlled by an external interface rather than by the internal command engine.
- Dedicated error and SPI-event interrupt outputs.
- Alert reporting for register-interface integrity errors.

## 2. Reset and Initialization

### 2.1 Power-On Reset

After reset:

- The command engine must be in an idle state.
- The command queue must be empty.
- The TX and RX data FIFOs must be empty.
- SPI outputs must be placed in an inactive state:
  - SCK must be at its configured idle polarity.
  - All chip-select outputs must be deasserted high.
  - Data-line output enables must be deasserted so that data lines are not driven by the module.
- Interrupt outputs must be deasserted.
- Alert outputs must be deasserted unless an alert-test request is active.

### 2.2 Software Reset

A software reset must:

- Clear the command queue.
- Clear the TX and RX FIFOs.
- Return the command engine to idle.
- Deassert SPI activity.
- Preserve control, configuration, status, interrupt, and error registers that are not otherwise cleared by software.

Software reset is intended to provide a clean reset of the SPI execution path without resetting the register programming model.

### 2.3 Enabling SPI Operation

The module must not begin executing commands or generating SPI bus activity until software has set the SPI enable bit in the control register.

When the SPI enable bit is cleared:

- The command engine must suspend operation.
- Any transaction that was already submitted must remain pending.
- When the SPI enable bit is set again, execution must resume from the suspended point.

The SPI output drivers must not be enabled until the output-enable bit is set. When output enable is cleared, the module must deassert the output-enable signals for SCK, chip-select, and data lines, so the SPI pins are not driven by the module.

## 3. Configuration

### 3.1 Per-Device Configuration

The module must provide configuration settings for each chip-select output. These settings control:

- SPI clock divider.
- Minimum chip-select idle time before a transaction.
- Minimum chip-select lead time after assertion before the first SCK edge.
- Minimum chip-select trail time after the last SCK edge before deassertion.
- Clock polarity (CPOL).
- Clock phase (CPHA).
- Full-cycle receive sampling mode.

Each command segment must use the configuration associated with the chip-select ID selected for that segment.

### 3.2 Configuration Changes

Configuration changes must take effect only while all chip-select lines are deasserted high. The module must not produce spurious SCK edges or other activity when a configuration change is applied.

If a configuration change is requested after a transaction that had chip-select held active, the module must first close out that transaction, deassert the chip-select line, and only then apply the new configuration.

The module must also preserve a minimum chip-select idle time both before and after the configuration change. The required idle time must satisfy both the old configuration’s idle requirement and the new configuration’s idle requirement.

## 4. Command Processing

### 4.1 Segment Descriptors

Software issues SPI operations by writing segment descriptors. Each segment descriptor must specify:

- Segment length.
- Segment speed: Standard, Dual, or Quad.
- Segment direction: TX only, RX only, dummy, or bidirectional.
- Whether the chip-select line remains asserted after the segment (chip-select active after transaction).

Only Standard-speed segments may be bidirectional. Dual- and Quad-speed segments must be TX only, RX only, or dummy.

### 4.2 Command Acceptance and Queueing

The module must provide a command queue so that software can submit multiple segment descriptors without waiting for each segment to complete.

The module must expose:

- A ready status indicating whether the command queue can accept another segment descriptor.
- A command-queue depth status indicating how many descriptors are currently queued.
- An active status indicating whether the command engine is currently executing a segment.

Writing a segment descriptor when the command queue is not ready must be reported as an error and must not execute the descriptor.

### 4.3 Segment Execution

Each segment must be executed serially in the order it was written.

For a TX segment:

- The module must transmit bytes from the TX FIFO on the active data lines.
- Input data on the receive data lines must be ignored.

For an RX segment:

- The module must receive bytes from the active data lines and place them into the RX FIFO.
- Data output drivers must be deasserted for the receive data lines.

For a dummy segment:

- SCK must toggle for the specified segment length.
- No data must be transmitted and no data must be captured.
- All data-line output drivers must be deasserted.

For a bidirectional Standard-speed segment:

- The module must transmit one byte from the TX FIFO on the transmit data line while simultaneously receiving one byte on the receive data line.
- The RX FIFO must receive one byte for each byte transmitted.

### 4.4 Chip-Select Operation

During a segment, the module must assert the chip-select line corresponding to the chip-select ID associated with the segment. All other chip-select lines must remain deasserted.

If the chip-select ID is outside the valid range for the configured number of chip-select outputs, the module must report a chip-select-ID error and must not execute the segment.

### 4.5 Multi-Segment Transactions

When a segment descriptor has chip-select-active-after-transaction asserted, the chip-select line must remain asserted after the end of the segment. This allows the next segment to continue the same SPI transaction.

If the next segment is already queued when the current segment ends, the module must begin the next segment without deasserting chip-select.

If no next segment is queued, the module must wait with chip-select asserted until a new segment is submitted. During this wait, SCK must remain at its idle polarity.

If a segment is submitted with chip-select-active-after-transaction deasserted, the module must end the transaction after the segment:

- Hold SCK inactive.
- Keep the chip-select line asserted for the configured trail time.
- Deassert the chip-select line.
- Hold all chip-select lines deasserted for the configured idle time before the next transaction.

### 4.6 Changing Target Device

When a new segment descriptor selects a different chip-select ID from the previous segment, the module must treat that as an implicit end of the previous transaction, even if the previous segment requested chip-select-active-after-transaction.

The previous transaction must be closed out with the configured trail and idle timing. The new segment must then be executed on the newly selected chip-select line with the appropriate lead timing.

### 4.7 Queueing Commands While Active

The command queue must allow new segment descriptors to be submitted while the command engine is active, provided the queue has space.

The ready status must indicate whether the queue has space, independent of whether a segment is currently executing.

## 5. SPI Clock Generation

### 5.1 Clock Divider

The module must generate SCK from the module input clock using the configured clock divider for the selected chip-select.

SCK must have a 50% duty cycle. Each SCK half-period must be equal to the configured clock divider value plus one input-clock period.

### 5.2 Clock Polarity

When CPOL is 0, SCK must idle low and active pulses must be high.

When CPOL is 1, SCK must idle high and active pulses must be low.

SCK must not toggle while no segment is being executed.

### 5.3 Clock Phase and Data Timing

For CPHA = 0:

- The first transmitted bit must be driven when the chip-select line is asserted, before the first SCK edge.
- Transmitted bits must change on the trailing edge of SCK.
- Received bits must be sampled on the leading edge of SCK.

For CPHA = 1:

- Transmitted bits must change on the leading edge of SCK.
- Received bits must be sampled on the trailing edge of SCK.

The meanings of “leading” and “trailing” depend on the configured CPOL value.

### 5.4 Full-Cycle Receive Timing

When full-cycle mode is enabled, the module must delay the receive sampling point by one full SCK cycle relative to the normal sampling point.

This mode affects only the sampling of received data. It must not change the timing or value of transmitted signals.

## 6. Chip-Select Timing

### 6.1 Lead, Trail, and Idle Delays

The module must implement minimum timing delays around chip-select edges.

- Lead time: the minimum delay between the assertion of the selected chip-select line and the first leading edge of SCK.
- Trail time: the minimum delay between the last trailing edge of SCK and the deassertion of the selected chip-select line.
- Idle time: the minimum delay between the deassertion of one chip-select line and the assertion of any chip-select line for the next transaction.

Each delay must be at least one SCK half-period plus the value programmed in the corresponding configuration field. Actual delays may be longer due to internal synchronization and command processing.

### 6.2 Extended Idle During Configuration Changes

When a configuration change is detected, the module must extend the inter-transaction idle time to satisfy both the old configuration and the new configuration:

- Before applying the new configuration, the previously selected chip-select line must have been high for at least the old idle time.
- After applying the new configuration, the chip-select line must remain high for at least the new idle time before the next chip-select assertion.

## 7. Data FIFOs and Data Formatting

### 7.1 TX FIFO

The module must provide a TX data FIFO.

Software writes 32-bit data words into the TX FIFO through the register interface. Writes may include byte-enable information so that a word can contain one, two, or four valid bytes.

The module must accept:

- Single-byte writes.
- Contiguous two-byte writes.
- Four-byte full-word writes.

Any other byte-enable pattern must be rejected as an invalid access and must not be stored in the TX FIFO.

If software writes to the TX FIFO when it is full, the write must be ignored and an overflow error must be reported.

The module must expose the current TX FIFO fill level, empty status, full status, and watermark status.

### 7.2 RX FIFO

The module must provide an RX data FIFO.

Received bytes are packed into 32-bit words and placed into the RX FIFO.

If a receive segment produces a partial word, the remaining byte lanes in that word must be zero-padded before the word is placed into the RX FIFO.

If software reads from the RX FIFO when it is empty, the read must be ignored and an underflow error must be reported.

The module must expose the current RX FIFO fill level, empty status, full status, and watermark status.

### 7.3 Byte Ordering

The byte ordering used by the FIFOs must be fixed at configuration time.

In little-endian mode:

- The least-significant byte of a TX FIFO word must be transmitted first.
- The first byte received must be placed in the least-significant byte of an RX FIFO word.

In big-endian mode:

- The most-significant byte of a TX FIFO word must be transmitted first.
- The first byte received must be placed in the most-significant byte of an RX FIFO word.

Within each byte, the most-significant bit must be transmitted first and received first.

### 7.4 Partial TX Words

If a TX or bidirectional segment ends before the current TX FIFO word is fully consumed, the unused bytes from that word must be discarded. They must not be carried over to the next segment.

### 7.5 Data-Line Bit Ordering for Dual and Quad Modes

In Dual mode:

- Two bits are transferred per SCK edge.
- The less significant bit must be driven on the lower-numbered data line and the more significant bit on the higher-numbered data line.
- The same ordering applies to received bits.

In Quad mode:

- Four bits are transferred per SCK edge.
- The least significant bit must be driven on SD[0], with increasing significance on SD[1], SD[2], and SD[3].
- The same ordering applies to received bits.

### 7.6 Stalls

The module must stall SCK generation when:

- A TX or bidirectional segment needs more TX data but the TX FIFO is empty.
- An RX or bidirectional segment needs to receive more data but the RX FIFO is full and cannot accept another word.

During a stall:

- SCK must stop at its inactive level.
- The chip-select line must remain in its current state.
- The module must report the corresponding stall status.
- When the stall condition is removed, the module must resume SCK generation and data transfer.

Stall status must be read-only and must not by itself generate an interrupt.

## 8. Error Reporting and Error Interrupts

### 8.1 Error Status Register

The module must provide a sticky error status register with one bit for each error class. Software must clear each bit by writing 1 to it.

The following conditions must set the corresponding error status bit:

- Writing a segment descriptor when the command queue is not ready.
- Writing to the TX FIFO when it is full.
- Reading from the RX FIFO when it is empty.
- Writing a segment descriptor with an invalid speed or direction combination, such as a bidirectional Dual or Quad segment.
- Writing a segment descriptor with a chip-select ID greater than or equal to the number of chip-select outputs.
- Writing to the TX FIFO with an unsupported byte-enable pattern.

### 8.2 Halting on Error

While any error status bit is set, the module must suspend command execution.

During suspension:

- No new SPI segment may start.
- SCK must remain inactive.
- Chip-select lines must remain in their current state.
- The command engine must remain halted until software clears all error status bits.

Error-status reporting must continue even if the corresponding error interrupt is disabled.

### 8.3 Error Interrupt Generation

The module must provide an error interrupt output.

The error interrupt must be asserted when an error event occurs and that error class is enabled to produce an interrupt.

The “invalid access” error class must always produce an error interrupt; it must not be maskable through the error-enable register.

The error-enable register must affect only interrupt generation. It must not affect whether the error status bit is set or whether the command engine is halted.

## 9. SPI Event Reporting and Event Interrupts

### 9.1 Event Conditions

The module must provide an SPI-event interrupt output.

This interrupt must be generated when an enabled event condition transitions from false to true.

The module must support the following event conditions:

- The module becomes idle, meaning the command engine finishes a segment and no transaction is active.
- The command queue becomes ready to accept another segment descriptor.
- The TX FIFO becomes empty.
- The TX FIFO fill level falls below the configured TX watermark.
- The RX FIFO fill level reaches or exceeds the configured RX watermark.
- The RX FIFO becomes full.

Each event condition must have a separate enable bit. Disabled event conditions must not cause the SPI-event interrupt to be asserted.

### 9.2 Status Flags

The module must expose live status flags for the same conditions, so software can poll them:

- Active status.
- Ready status.
- TX FIFO empty and full.
- RX FIFO empty and full.
- TX watermark status.
- RX watermark status.
- TX stall and RX stall status.

These status flags must reflect current state and are not affected by event-enable settings.

## 10. Interrupt State and Testing

The module must provide standard interrupt state and interrupt test behavior for both interrupt outputs:

- The interrupt state register must record that an interrupt condition occurred.
- Interrupt state bits must be cleared by software writing 1.
- Interrupt test bits must allow software to force the corresponding interrupt state bit and interrupt output.
- Interrupt enable bits must gate the interrupt outputs.

An interrupt output must be asserted only when the corresponding interrupt state bit is set and the corresponding interrupt enable bit is set, or when an interrupt test is requested.

## 11. Alert Reporting

The module must detect register-interface integrity errors, such as TL-UL bus integrity failures.

When an integrity error is detected, the module must assert the alert output or outputs.

All alert outputs must report the same integrity error condition, but each alert output must also support an independent software test trigger.

Alert generation must not be gated by interrupt-enable or event-enable settings.

## 12. Pass-Through Operation

The module must provide a pass-through interface that allows an external controller to drive the SPI outputs directly.

When pass-through mode is enabled:

- SCK output must be driven from the pass-through interface rather than from the internal command engine.
- Chip-select outputs must be driven from the pass-through interface.
- Data-line outputs and data-line output enables must be driven from the pass-through interface.
- The internal command engine must not drive the SPI outputs.

The module must continuously present the received data-line values on the pass-through response interface, regardless of whether pass-through mode is enabled.

Pass-through mode must override the normal SPI output enables. In pass-through mode, the global SPI output-enable bit must not gate the SPI output enables; the pass-through interface supplies them.

Pass-through operation is defined only for configurations with a single chip-select output. In configurations with more than one chip-select output, pass-through requests must be ignored and must not affect the SPI outputs.

Pass-through mode must not require the SPI enable bit to be set. It must also remain active across software reset of the internal command engine, because it is independent of command execution.

## 13. Status Reporting

The module must provide a read-only status register containing:

- The fixed byte-order setting, so software can confirm the configured data ordering.
- Command-engine active state.
- Command-queue ready state.
- TX FIFO fill level.
- RX FIFO fill level.
- Command-queue fill level.
- TX FIFO empty, full, and watermark flags.
- RX FIFO empty, full, and watermark flags.
- TX stall and RX stall flags.

All status fields must reflect current state and must be updated continuously while the module is running.
